hooks.spoken: Sixteen years. That's how long this bug sat inside your server's firmware.
Your servers can get owned before the operating system even boots.
The scariest code on your server runs before your security tools wake up.

beats.text: Sixteen years. That's how long this bug sat inside your server's firmware.

A buffer overflow in the network boot code of TianoCore EDK2, the base for most UEFI firmware, lets an attacker on the network run code on a server before the operating system loads. And it's reportedly already being exploited.

Here's the trick. When a server boots over the network, it trusts the packets telling it where to load from. Send one longer than the buffer expects and you overwrite memory the firmware is running. The catch: the attacker needs the server's IP and firmware build.
Nothing on the box can see it, because it runs before the OS. And patching firmware means downtime, so these servers stay exposed for months.
Somewhere, a server is booting someone else's code right now.

post.caption: This firmware bug sat in most servers for 16 years. Your EDR can't even see it.
post.pinned_comment: Patching UEFI needs a reboot window. How long does your org take to schedule one?
